rp_note: Enterococci is not evaluated by a calculated RWC. Both PRWQS criteria are frequency- and interval-based — a geometric mean over any 90-day interval (35/100 mL) and the 90th percentile of samples over that same interval (130/100 mL) — and neither is a maximum concentration to which a multiplying-factor projection can be meaningfully applied. Reported values are compared directly to the criteria. DMR geometric means are commonly 30-day or monthly rather than 90-day, and dilution is not applied. The permit writer should evaluate the geometric mean and the 90th percentile over the applicable 90-day intervals independently before concluding on reasonable potential.

Dissolved oxygen is evaluated by direct comparison of the observed minimum to the criterion; no RWC is calculated. A defensible DO analysis requires the Streeter-Phelps equation, whose inputs (reaeration and deoxygenation rates, travel time, upstream deficit) are not available in ICIS-NPDES. Where no excursion is observed the determination is DEPENDS, not NO: the permit writer should determine whether additional data must be collected to apply Streeter-Phelps.

PRWQS surfactant criteria are expressed as substances reactive with methylene blue (MBAS). Permittees report under either 47021 (methylene blue active substances) or 38260 (surfactants [MBAS]); both are crosswalked to the same criteria. Class SG requires that they not be present, evaluated as a detection test.

The PRWQS temperature criterion applies in the receiving water — a discharge shall not cause the temperature at any site to exceed 30 C — not at the point of discharge. An end-of-pipe comparison is therefore screening only. Where no excursion is observed the determination is DEPENDS: the permit writer should evaluate in-stream temperature and the applicable mixing zone before concluding on reasonable potential.
